b1-adj-sinnvoll: Your friend wants to buy a winter coat in July at full price. You say waiting for the end-of-season sale would be a much wiser plan. How do you describe such a plan?
After a long meeting you tell a colleague that it was useful and worth your time, not a waste at all. Which word describes something that has a good purpose?
Your teacher says you should spend your free hour on something that really helps you, not just play games. Which word means 'sensible'?
b1-n-praktikantin: At the office, a young woman is working for three months to learn the job. She is not a real employee yet. Who is she?
A girl spends her summer holiday in a bakery to get work experience. Her boss introduces her to you. What do you call her?
A young woman helps the nurses at the hospital as part of her training. Which word means 'intern' for a woman?
b1-v-funktionieren: You press the button on your new coffee machine, but nothing happens. You tell your flatmate that the machine does not ...
Your phone was broken last week, but after the repair it runs as it should again. You tell your friend: 'Now it ...!'
Your boss asks if the new plan will succeed in real life. You answer that you hope it will do what it is supposed to do.
b1-n-mappe: You keep your bank papers in a thin cardboard cover with a flap on your desk. What is it?
An art student carries a big flat case with her drawings to show them at the university interview.
At the office, you put the signed contract into a plastic cover with a coloured spine. Which word means 'folder' for papers?
b1-n-erziehung: Parents teach their child to say please and thank you and to be polite. This long process of raising a child is called what?
A woman says she is grateful to her parents for the strong values they gave her when she was growing up.
A teacher says that the way children are brought up at home is as important as school. Which word means 'upbringing'?
b1-v-klopfen: Someone stands outside your room and gently hits the door with their knuckles before coming in. What do they do?
The doctor taps on your back with her fingers while listening to your chest.
After running up the stairs, you feel your heart hitting hard and fast in your chest.
b1-n-produktion: A car factory makes 500 cars every day. What do we call the process of making goods in large numbers?
The company wants to increase the making of goods in its factory by twenty percent next year.
b1-adj-relativ: You say the flat is quite cheap, but only when you compare it with other flats in the city. It is ... cheap.
Your friend says nothing is big or small by itself; it all depends on what you compare it with. Everything is ...
The test was fairly easy compared with last year's test. Which word means 'relative'?
b1-n-pension: On holiday in the mountains you stay in a small family-run place with breakfast, cheaper than a big hotel. What is it?
Your parents are visiting and want a cosy, simple place to sleep, run by a friendly family, not a big hotel.
b1-v-zusagen: A friend invites you to her birthday party and you reply that yes, you will come. What do you do to the invitation?
The company offers you a job and you tell them you gladly take it. You ... the offer.
Your boss asks if you can finish by Friday and you give your word that you will.
b1-n-kneipe: In the evening you meet friends at a small, simple place with a bar where you drink beer and the regulars know each other.
After football the team goes to a casual local place to have a drink, not a restaurant.
b1-n-spezialist: Your doctor cannot treat your rare skin problem, so he sends you to a man who knows everything about that one narrow field.
The IT company hires a man who only deals with network security and nothing else.
b1-n-kassette: Your grandfather has an old plastic box with magnetic tape inside that he plays in his old music player.
Before phones and CDs, you recorded songs from the radio onto a small tape in a plastic case.
b1-adj-oekologisch: At the market you buy vegetables that were grown without chemicals and with care for nature.
A company builds houses that protect the environment and use little energy.
b1-v-bremsen: You ride your bike down a hill and a child runs across the road. You squeeze the handles to stop.
The driver sees a red light and presses the pedal to make the car slower.
b1-n-vortrag: A professor stands in front of 200 students and speaks for an hour about climate change with slides.
At work you must speak to your team about last year's sales next Monday. You prepare your slides.
b1-adv-anfangs: Your German course was difficult in the first weeks, but now it is fine. You tell your friend that ... it was hard.
You did not like the city in the early days, but later you loved it.
b1-n-strumpf: A woman wears something thin and sheer on her legs under her skirt, going up to the knee or higher.
It is a cold day. You put on a long, thin garment over your foot and leg, under your boots.
b1-v-sich-naehern: A train is coming closer to the station. You hear it getting louder and louder.
Dark clouds are moving toward the town and a storm is about to start.
A shy boy slowly walks toward the girl at the party to say hello. Which word means 'to approach'?
b1-n-tat: The police are looking for the man who did the bad thing at the shop last night. They find clues at the scene.
The mayor says he will not just talk, he wants to do something real. People want to see his actions.
b1-adj-mobil: You use your phone while walking in the park. It does not need a cable or a fixed place.
A doctor with a special van can go to patients anywhere in the region.
Your elderly neighbour can still walk and move around by himself. Which word means 'mobile'?
b1-n-limonade: On a hot day, kids sell a sweet, fizzy, yellow drink made with lemons at a stand.
At the café you order a cold sparkling lemon-flavoured soft drink for your child.
b1-n-quittung: After paying the plumber in cash, you ask for a piece of paper that proves you paid.
You bought a printer for your company and the accountant needs paper showing the payment.
b1-v-auffuehren: The school children will show a play on stage in front of their parents on Friday.
The accountant writes each item one under another in the report, one by one.
The theatre will put on a famous play on Saturday evening.
b1-n-feld: A farmer walks across a big area of land where wheat is growing.
On the tax form you write your name in a small empty space.
Football players run on a green area with two goals. Which word could describe this area, or a pitch?
b1-n-muecke: On a summer night, a tiny flying insect bites your arm and makes a high buzzing sound near your ear.
By the lake you put on spray to keep away small flying insects that bite.
b1-adj-steil: The road up the mountain goes sharply upward, almost like a wall. You have to push your bike.
The stairs in the old tower are almost vertical and hard to climb.
b1-v-sich-amuesieren: At the party you dance, laugh and have a great time with your friends.
After a long week of work, you go to the fun fair and enjoy yourself.
Your friend asks about the concert: 'Did you enjoy yourself?' Which verb do you need?
b1-n-beweis: The detective needs something that shows the suspect was at the scene, such as a fingerprint.
Your friend does not believe you. You show him a photo to show that it is true.
b1-n-vase: You bought a bunch of flowers and put them in a glass container with water on the table.
Your aunt gives you a pretty ceramic container for your roses.
b1-v-aufladen: Your phone is at 5 percent, so you plug it in.
You put money onto your bus card at the machine.
At the warehouse you put the boxes onto the truck.
b1-n-sicherheit: You put on your seatbelt in the car to protect yourself from danger.
A bank has guards and cameras to protect it against thieves.
The doctor says she cannot be sure yet whether your arm is broken. She cannot say it with ...
b1-n-rueckfahrt: You spent a weekend at the sea. On Sunday evening you drive back home and the traffic is heavy.
You need a ticket for going to Munich and another one for going back.
b1-adj-froehlich: The children sing and laugh in the garden. They are in a very good mood.
Your colleague always greets everyone with a big smile and a happy voice.
b1-adv-los: Your friend looks very sad. You ask what is the matter: 'What is ... with you?'
You finally got rid of your old cold and feel free of it. You are ... the cold.
At the start of the race the starter says everybody can go now. Which word do you hear?
b1-n-kandidat: In the election, a man puts his name forward to be chosen as mayor.
A man is applying for the job and the manager is interviewing him today.
On a quiz show, a man sits on the stage and answers the questions. Which word means 'candidate' or 'contestant'?
b1-v-giessen: Your plants are dry. You take a can and give them some water.
You carefully pour milk from the jug into the glass.
b1-n-tempo: A sign on the motorway shows the maximum speed. You drive at the right speed.
During the marathon, a runner keeps a steady pace for two hours.
You have a cold and ask your neighbour for a paper handkerchief, often called by a brand name.
b1-n-radfahrer: A car driver must watch out for a man on a bicycle at the crossing.
In the Tour de France, a man pedals up the mountain with a helmet.
b1-v-beschliessen: After a long discussion the city council votes and makes a final choice to build a new park.
You finally make up your mind: you will learn German every day.
The group decides together to go on holiday in August. Which word means 'to decide'?
b1-adj-persoenlich: Your boss does not want to discuss it by email. He asks you to come in and talk face to face.
You write a private letter about your own feelings, not a business letter.
b1-n-liebe: A couple holds hands and feels strong, deep affection for each other.
A mother looks at her baby with a warm, caring feeling.
b1-n-pfanne: You want to fry eggs, so you take a flat, round metal pot with a long handle.
You put oil in it and heat it on the stove to fry fish.
b1-v-ersetzen: The lamp is broken, so you buy a new one to take its place.
The company paid you back the money you spent on the train ticket.
A new teacher takes the place of the teacher who retired.
b1-n-nadel: Your grandmother sews a button on with a thin, sharp piece of steel with a hole for the thread.
At the doctor's, a thin, sharp point goes into your arm for the injection.
b1-n-scheibe: You cut the cheese and put one thin flat piece on your bread.
A bird flew into the window and the sheet of glass cracked.
b1-adj-traditionell: At Christmas your family always cooks the same dish, as it was handed down over generations.
People wear old national clothes at the village festival, as they have done for ages.
b1-n-wissen: Grandma has so much information in her head from many years of reading and living.
In a quiz test, the teacher checks what you have learned and what you know.
b1-v-fassen: The child takes your hand and holds it tightly. He ... your hand.
After a long chase the police finally catch the thief.
The bottle can contain one litre of water. Which verb fits?
b1-n-vitamin: The doctor says orange juice contains lots of C, an important substance the body needs in tiny amounts.
In winter you take small tablets from the pharmacy to stay healthy and avoid a cold.
b1-adv-zwar: You admit one fact before adding a 'but': 'The room is ... clean, but it is very small.'
A friend says: 'The film was ... long, but I liked it.' Which small word admits a point before the 'but'?
b1-n-wand: You hang a picture on the vertical side of your living room.
The painter paints the sides of the bedroom white.
Which word means 'wall' inside a room?
b1-v-anerkennen: Your boss says your work is excellent and shows he values your effort.
Germany officially accepts your university degree from abroad as valid.
After losing the match, he admits the other player was better. He ... it.
b1-adj-voellig: After the exam you are not partly tired but entirely exhausted. You are ... tired.
You have not just half forgotten the meeting, you have forgotten it all.
b1-n-kuvert: You write a letter and put it into a paper cover, then add a stamp and post it.
At a wedding you give money to the couple in a small paper pouch.
b1-n-wettervorhersage: Before a picnic you check the TV to see if it will rain tomorrow.
In the evening news a woman shows a map with sun and cloud symbols for the next days.
b1-n-sahne: You whip the white, thick liquid made from milk and put it on top of the cake.
At the café you ask for your hot chocolate with a thick white topping.
b1-v-verwenden: In the recipe, you take fresh herbs, not dried ones. You ... fresh herbs.
You choose a special pen for signing the contract.
b1-n-reservierung: Before going to the popular restaurant, you phone to get a table for Friday evening.
On the long train trip, you book a seat so you do not have to stand.
b1-adj-befreit: Students do not have to pay the fee. They are excused from it.
The prisoner is no longer locked up and feels liberated.
After handing in your thesis, you feel free of a heavy burden. Which word means 'exempt' or 'free'?
b1-n-kommunikation: In your job, good talking and listening between team members is very important.
Phones, emails and messages are all ways of exchanging information between people.
b1-v-einzahlen: You go to the bank counter and put cash into your account.
At the machine you pay money into your savings account.
b1-n-kopierer: At the office you put a sheet of paper into a machine and get ten copies.
At the library, the machine that makes paper copies is out of toner.
b1-n-rueckmeldung: After your presentation, the teacher tells you what went well and what could be better.
You sent an email to your landlord and are now waiting for an answer.
b1-v-runterfahren: At the end of the day, you switch off your computer in the correct way.
The factory reduces production to save energy.
Which word means 'to shut down' a computer?
b1-n-ueberraschung: Friends hide in the dark and shout when you walk into your birthday party.
You open a box and find an unexpected gift.
b1-adj-einheitlich: All the workers in the factory wear the same blue clothes.
The whole school follows the same rules and nothing differs between classes.
b1-adv-neulich: You tell a friend that you saw a film a few days ago. You don't remember the exact day.
You say you met his sister at the supermarket not long ago.
b1-n-mehrwertsteuer: On the receipt there is a line showing 19 percent extra tax added to the price of the goods.
A tourist asks how to get back the tax that was added to the price of her goods.
b1-n-recherche: A journalist spends weeks looking for facts before writing an article.
A student searches the library and the internet for sources for his essay.
b1-v-zugehen: The shy girl walks up to the new student to say hello. She wants to ... him.
The old door does not shut properly, even if you push it.
A man walks toward you with open arms.
b1-n-couch: In the living room you relax on a soft piece of furniture for several people, with cushions.
A guest stays overnight and sleeps on it.
b1-adj-ewig: A couple promises to love each other until the end of time.
Waiting at the airport, it felt like it lasted forever.
b1-n-tourismus: The coast earns a lot of money from visitors who come on holiday every summer.
A student studies the business of travel, hotels and sightseeing.
b1-v-gelten: Your ticket is good for one day only. After that it is no longer ...
The rule applies to everyone, even the boss.
He is regarded as the best player in the team.
b1-n-zeile: In your notebook, you write one horizontal row of words under another, like a poem.
The teacher says: 'Look at the fifth one in the text and read it aloud.'
In a spreadsheet, you sum the numbers across a horizontal row.
b1-n-gott: In many religions, people pray to a powerful male being who created the world.
In old Greek myths, Zeus is one of these powerful male beings.
b1-n-muskel: After the gym, the part of your arm that lets you lift things is sore.
The doctor says you pulled a part in your leg while running.
b1-v-tanken: The red light on the dashboard shows the car is almost empty, so you stop at a petrol station.
On the motorway you put fuel into your car.
Which word means 'to fill up' a car?
b1-adj-wild: In the forest you see an animal that is not tamed and lives free.
The party was crazy, with loud music and a lot of dancing.
The garden has been left alone and grows freely and untidily.
b1-n-kostuem: At carnival, people dress up as pirates and witches.
A woman wears a matching business jacket and skirt to the interview.
b1-n-treppenhaus: In an apartment building, you hear your neighbours' voices in the shared space with steps between the floors.
The fire alarm goes off and everyone leaves through the enclosed space with stairs.
b1-adv-eher: Your friend asks if you want to go out or stay in. You say you would rather stay at home.
You ask which is more likely: that it rains or that it snows.
You think you can arrive sooner than the others.
b1-v-verbrennen: You put old letters into the fire and watch them turn to ash.
The city waste plant destroys rubbish with very high heat.
You forgot the toast in the toaster and now it is black. Which verb means 'to burn'?
b1-n-bildschirm: Your computer has a flat part that shows the picture and you want a bigger one.
At the airport, a panel shows the flight times.
b1-n-wunder: The doctor says it is almost unbelievable that the patient survived. Nobody can explain it.
A guidebook lists seven amazing things of the world.
b1-adj-hoeflich: A boy holds the door for you and says please and thank you.
The shop assistant speaks kindly and respectfully to every customer.
b1-v-schweigen: The teacher asks who broke the window, but nobody says anything.
In the library you must not talk and everybody is quiet.
He decides not to answer the police's questions.
b1-n-kasten: You carry a crate of mineral water bottles up to your flat.
You pack your books into a big box before moving house.
b1-n-vorstellung: The theatre play starts at eight and you buy tickets for tonight's show.
At the new job, the colleagues tell each other their names. Everyone does a short self-introduction.
You have no picture in your mind of what the new office looks like. You have no ... of it.
b1-n-haelfte: You cut the cake into two equal parts and eat one of them.
The footballers get a break after the first 45 minutes of the match.
b1-v-vorkommen: Such mistakes happen sometimes, even to experts.
The story seems strange to you, as if you have heard it before.
This word appears often in the text.
b1-adj-aehnlich: Twin sisters look almost the same but not identical.
Your phone and mine are almost the same model.
b1-n-eindruck: After the first meeting you tell your friend what you think of the new colleague.
At the interview you want to make a good first impression on the manager.
b1-n-form: A cookie cutter makes biscuits in the shape of a star.
The baker pours dough into a metal tin to bake a cake.
Circle, square and triangle are different ones. Which word means 'shape'?
b1-v-stinken: The old fish in the fridge makes a terrible smell.
Your gym socks smell horribly bad.
The rubbish bin gives off a bad smell on a hot day.
b1-n-abbildung: In the textbook there is a drawing next to the text with the caption 'Fig. 3'.
The brochure has nice photos of the hotel.
Which word means 'illustration' or 'image' in a book?
b1-n-knie: The joint in the middle of your leg hurts after running.
The child fell and scraped the joint between thigh and shin.
b1-adj-statistisch: The study shows numbers collected on how many people use the bus each day.
According to the office's numbers, an average person eats a lot of bread each year.
b1-adv-kaum: There is almost no one in the cinema. Only two people are there.
You can scarcely hear your friend because the music is so loud.
